> **What this case shows** — sample entropy asks a yes/no question of every pair of templates: do they
> match within tolerance *r*? That **crisp Heaviside step** makes it brittle on short or noisy data —
> a template just past the threshold counts for nothing. **Fuzzy entropy** (Chen et al. 2007) softens
> the step into a smooth membership **exp(−d/r)**, so near-matches count *partially*. This case
> introduces a **newly-authored op**, `fuzzyEntropy`, completing the ecosystem's sample-entropy family.
> On a real eyes-closed EEG channel it reproduces `NeuroKit2.entropy_fuzzy` **bit-for-bit** (max |diff|
> ~**4e-15**), and shows the consequence: at m = 2, FuzzyEn (**0.948**) sits below the crisp sample
> entropy (**1.327**) — the soft membership simply counts more.

::: {.callout-tip title="The recipe you'll learn"}
**Workflow** — `fuzzyEntropy(x, dimension, r)` → the fuzzy entropy of the signal.
**Way of thinking** — a hard threshold throws away information at its boundary. A soft membership keeps
it. When a complexity measure is unstable on your data, ask whether a *fuzzy* version exists — it
usually trades a sharp cutoff for a graded one and gains robustness.
**Ecosystem usage** — `PhysioEEG::fuzzyEntropy()` (fuzzy) alongside the crisp sample/approximate
entropies; `dimension = 2`, `r = 0.2` are the standard defaults.
:::

## Proposition

On real eyes-closed POz EEG, `fuzzyEntropy` reproduces `NeuroKit2.entropy_fuzzy` bit-for-bit (max
|diff| ~4e-15) across (dimension, r); at m = 2, r = 0.2 FuzzyEn (0.948) is lower than the crisp sample
entropy (1.327), and it is non-increasing in the embedding dimension.

## Question & goal

**The question is a gap and a mechanism: the ecosystem had the crisp sample/approximate entropies but
not the fuzzy generalization — can we author it, reproduce the reference, and show what the soft
membership changes?** The goal is to introduce `fuzzyEntropy`, certify it bit-for-bit, and make the
fuzzy-vs-crisp relationship concrete.

## Challenge & approach

Fuzzy entropy embeds the signal, removes each vector's local baseline, takes Chebyshev distances, and
weights matches by exp(−(d^n)/r) (with r = 0.2·sd) instead of the crisp I(d < r); then
FuzzyEn = −ln(φ_{m+1}/φ_m). We implement that exactly and check it against `NeuroKit2.entropy_fuzzy`
across (m, r), and — on the same signal — compare against the crisp sample entropy.

```
EEG POz (eegmmidb) → embed, baseline-remove → Chebyshev d → weight exp(−d/r) → FuzzyEn = −ln(φ_{m+1}/φ_m)
                    vs NeuroKit2.entropy_fuzzy (same pipeline) → bit-exact (~4e-15) for every (m, r)
                    m=2: FuzzyEn 0.948 < crisp SampEn 1.327 (soft counts near-matches); monotonic in m
```

## Data

**EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database (eegmmidb, PhysioNet)**: subject **S002**, run **R02
(eyes-closed)**, channel **POz**, 10 s at 160 Hz — the same git-tracked vector the
[SVD-entropy](../svd-entropy-eegmmidb/index.qmd), [Petrosian](../petrosian-fd-eegmmidb/index.qmd),
[Renyi](../renyi-entropy-eegmmidb/index.qmd), [Tsallis](../tsallis-entropy-eegmmidb/index.qmd) and
[dispersion-entropy](../dispersion-entropy-eegmmidb/index.qmd) cases use. Details in
[`artifacts/data_sources.json`](artifacts/data_sources.json).

## Results

![Left: the two matching rules — fuzzy entropy's smooth membership exp(−d/r) (red) versus sample entropy's crisp step I(d < r) (blue). The soft curve gives partial credit to near-matches just beyond the threshold, which the step discards. Right: FuzzyEn (red) and the crisp SampEn (blue) across the embedding dimension — both decrease with m, but FuzzyEn sits consistently lower because it counts more (partial) matches.](artifacts/figure.png)

*How to read this:* the left panel is the mechanism (soft vs hard counting); the right panel is the
consequence (FuzzyEn < SampEn at every dimension, both monotonic). The op equals NeuroKit2 at every
setting.

| Quantity | Value |
|---|--:|
| **FuzzyEn, m = 2** (r = 0.2) | **0.948** |
| **FuzzyEn, m = 3** | **0.704** |
| op vs `NeuroKit2.entropy_fuzzy` (max \|diff\| over the family) | **4e-15** (bit-exact) |
| crisp **SampEn, m = 2** (same r) | **1.327** |
| \|FuzzyEn − SampEn\| at m = 2 | **0.38** |
| non-increasing in dimension | **yes** |

The newly-authored op equals NeuroKit2 at every setting, and is consistently lower than the crisp
sample entropy — the soft membership's signature. Values trace to
[`artifacts/fuzzy_summary.csv`](artifacts/fuzzy_summary.csv).

## Conclusion

`fuzzyEntropy` completes the sample-entropy family — the ecosystem now has both the crisp (SampEn) and
fuzzy (FuzzyEn) forms — and it is exact: bit-for-bit against NeuroKit2 across (m, r). The transferable
takeaway: **a crisp threshold is a modeling choice, not a law. Fuzzy entropy keeps the same
template-matching skeleton but grades the match, which is what makes it the go-to complexity measure
for short, noisy physiological segments where SampEn becomes unstable.**

## Open questions

- Fuzzy entropy's robustness makes it the natural core for multiscale fuzzy entropy (MFE): apply
  `fuzzyEntropy` to coarse-grained versions of the signal across scales, where crisp SampEn grows
  unstable at coarse scales. *Documented, not escalated.*

## Using this in your own analysis

| Step | Function | Package |
|---|---|---|
| Fuzzy entropy (soft membership) | `fuzzyEntropy()` | PhysioEEG |
| Dispersion entropy (NCDF symbolic dynamics) | `dispersionEntropy()` | PhysioEEG |
| Renyi / Tsallis entropy (amplitude histogram) | `renyiEntropy()`, `tsallisEntropy()` | PhysioEEG |
| multi-measure complexity (incl. crisp sample entropy) | `eegComplexity()` | PhysioEEG |

**Choosing the parameters.**

- **dimension** — embedding length *m* (default 2); larger m probes longer patterns but needs more data.
- **r** — tolerance as a fraction of the signal's sd (default 0.2, matching NeuroKit2's
  `tolerance = "sd"`); the distance tolerance is `r * sd(x)`.
- **n** — the fuzzy power (default 1); higher n sharpens the membership back toward the crisp step.
- **units** — dimensionless; nats-based log as in `NeuroKit2.entropy_fuzzy`.

**The recipe, copy-runnable:**

```r
library(PhysioEEG)

fuzzyEntropy(x, dimension = 2, r = 0.2)   # fuzzy generalization of sample entropy
# reproduces NeuroKit2.entropy_fuzzy bit-for-bit; lower than crisp SampEn at the same (m, r).
```

**Auditing the numbers.** Every value on this page traces to
[`artifacts/fuzzy_summary.csv`](artifacts/fuzzy_summary.csv), and [`audit.py`](audit.py) re-checks
FuzzyEn at m = 2 and m = 3, the bit-exact NeuroKit2 match over the (m, r) family, the crisp SampEn
reference and the fuzzy-vs-sample gap, the monotonicity, and the honestly-noted scope (newly-authored
op; machine-precision; value depends on m/r/n).
